stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates active community interest and performance tracking for a significant open-source LLM.

stories.title: Nvidia, Microsoft launch open AI security alliance — without OpenAI, Google, or Anthropic
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Nvidia and Microsoft are launching the Open Secure AI Alliance to develop and share open-source AI security tools.
The alliance includes major players like SpaceX and IBM, notably excluding OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic.
The initiative is a direct industry response to growing concerns regarding the safety and security risks posed by frontier AI models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its application in large language model tasks.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML components such as transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 introduces significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase when tested with the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for models.
The updated engine also contributes to higher quality outputs from the language models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
A key feature is its local-first architecture, allowing AI to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
It integrates native support for Ollama, simplifying the deployment of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing AI workloads for Apple hardware.
This is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Apple is banking on privacy to set its smart glasses apart
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly planning to unveil its first smart glasses at WWDC next June.
The anticipated launch window for Apple's smart glasses is set for the end of 2027.
A key differentiator for Apple's devices will be a strong focus on privacy features and messaging.

stories.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
stories.author: Joaquim Pina
bullet_points: Investigates the lack of stability and transparency in how major LLMs (Claude, Grok, GPT, Gemini) validate contested scientific claims.
The study specifically tests LLM responses to ethnonationalist pseudo-science across different model versions and timeframes.
Highlights a critical issue in AI deployment: how configuration choices (e.g., Grok's Fast versions) influence the model's epistemic stance.

stories.title: CausalForge: A Formally Grounded, Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Automated Research in Causal Inference
stories.author: Vasilis Syrgkanis
bullet_points: Introduces CausalForge, a new agentic framework designed for automated theoretical research in causal inference.
Addresses the critical weakness of current LLM reviewers, which are empirically unreliable at detecting fabricated research.
Grounds the framework in the Lean proof system to ensure formal correctness and self-improvement in the research loop.

stories.title: CausalForge: A Formally Grounded, Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Automated Research in Causal Inference
stories.author: Vasilis Syrgkanis
bullet_points: Introduces CausalForge, a new agentic framework designed to automate theoretical research specifically in causal inference.
Addresses the critical weakness of current LLM-based reviewers, which are often empirically unreliable in validating scientific claims.
Grounds the framework in the Lean proof system to ensure formal correctness and self-improvement in the research loop.

stories.title: Skill Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of LLM Capability with Co-Evolving Skills
stories.author: Guanjun Jiang
bullet_points: The research addresses a core challenge in LLM self-evolution: balancing task diversity with reliable feedback.
Existing methods are limited: environment-bound approaches are narrow, while open-ended generation lacks verification, risking reward pollution.
The paper proposes using 'agent skills' as a mechanism to push LLM capabilities through interaction-driven self-evolution.

stories.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science
stories.author: Joaquim Pina
bullet_points: Investigates the non-transparent and unstable nature of how major LLMs (Claude, Grok, GPT, Gemini) validate contested scientific claims.
Tests LLM responses to ethnonationalist pseudo-science across different model families and temporal snapshots.
Highlights deployment configuration (e.g., Grok's Fast versions) as a factor influencing LLM output and validation bias.

stories.title: DBA-Bench: A Production-Fidelity Benchmark for LLM-Based Database Operations Agents
stories.author: Kai Zheng
bullet_points: Introduces DBA-Bench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLM-based database operations agents with production-level fidelity.
Highlights critical gaps in current LLM evaluation, including lack of live-environment fidelity and complex observation spaces.
Addresses the need for benchmarks that account for solution-space openness, where multiple operational trade-offs exist for remediation.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now available via llama.cpp integration.
The update expands model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance Claude Code's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Meta is royally screwing up its smart glasses rollout
stories.author: Victoria Song
bullet_points: Meta's smart glasses rollout is facing public backlash, evidenced by satirical guerrilla advertising.
Activist groups are criticizing the technology, using slogans like 'biggest advancement in pervert technology since the trenchcoat.'
The controversy includes direct criticism of high-profile partners, such as Kylie Jenner, regarding the glasses' implications.

stories.title: Artist sues AI meme generator for selling deeply personal comic as ad template
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: An artist is suing an AI meme generator over the unauthorized use of a deeply personal comic in its advertising templates.
The core issue revolves around the AI model potentially reusing or misusing templates in its generated outputs.
The story highlights emerging legal and ethical concerns regarding AI data usage and intellectual property.

stories.title: SpaceX eyes tower catch for next Starship after auspicious end to 13th flight
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX plans to attempt a tower catch for the next Starship flight.
This follows the successful conclusion of the 13th Starship flight.
The maneuver aims to recover the vehicle near the launch pad.

stories.title: With help from data, art museums are reframing the visitor experience
stories.author: Mureji Fatunde-Iloeje
bullet_points: Art museums are integrating data analytics into their operational strategies.
The trend involves data-driven curation, changing how exhibits are presented and understood.
This shift reflects the broader impact of technology on cultural institutions.

stories.title: Big Tech accused of stonewalling European social media researchers
stories.author: Anna Desmarais, wired.com
bullet_points: Major social media platforms (TikTok, X, Meta) are facing accusations of non-compliance.
Researchers claim these tech giants are failing to provide data mandated by law.
The issue highlights ongoing friction between Big Tech and European regulatory/research bodies.

stories.title: Anthropic's Opus 5 is about token efficiency, not a capability leap
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Anthropic's Opus 5 focuses on improving token efficiency rather than achieving a massive leap in raw capability.
The article suggests that current, more cost-effective AI models are often sufficient for many practical applications.
This indicates a potential industry trend where efficiency and cost-effectiveness are becoming as important as peak performance in LLMs.

stories.title: SM4RT: Learning Structured Motion Geometry for 4D Reconstruction
stories.author: Jiwen Lu
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of extending 3D reconstruction to 4D dynamic understanding using Geometry Foundation Models (GFMs).
Existing motion perception methods are criticized for treating motion as independent point-wise displacements, ignoring physical structure.
The proposed method, SM4RT, aims to incorporate the structured nature of physical motion, such as rigid-body kinematics, into 4D reconstruction.

stories.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers
stories.author: Salvatore Venticinque
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for Explainable AI (XAI) in high-stakes environments.
It specifically focuses on applying Explainable Reinforcement Learning (RL) to assist Air Traffic Controllers.
The research aims to build trust and enable seamless human-AI collaboration in critical systems like aviation.

stories.title: The Regression Tax: Decomposing Why Skills Help and Hurt LLM Agents
stories.author: Baran Nama
bullet_points: The paper introduces the concept of the 'Regression Tax,' noting that adding procedural skills to LLM agents can sometimes degrade performance.
The research empirically measures both performance gains and performance losses (regressions) across extensive runs on office automation benchmarks.
This work provides a nuanced evaluation metric beyond simple task success rate, addressing the hidden costs of skill integration in LLM agents.

stories.title: \k{appa}-LoRA: Condition Numbers Reveal Which LoRA Matrices Worth Updating
stories.author: Yaqi Xie
bullet_points: The paper introduces $\kappa$-LoRA, a method to selectively update LoRA matrices during fine-tuning.
It addresses the computational inefficiency of standard LoRA, which updates all matrices uniformly.
The technique uses condition numbers to determine which low-rank matrices contribute most significantly to adaptation, enabling targeted updates.

stories.title: MineValiCoder: Reliable Code Generation with Test Case Quality Mining and Bipartite Graph-Based Mutual Validation
stories.author: Bo Li
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in LLM-based Test-Driven Development (TDD): reliance on human-crafted test cases.
Proposes 'MineValiCoder' to improve code generation reliability when only natural-language requirements are provided.
Mitigates issues arising from LLM stochasticity by using test case quality mining and bipartite graph validation.

stories.title: Learning to Prepare Molecular Ground States with Transformer Models
stories.author: Enrico Rinaldi
bullet_points: The research addresses the computational bottleneck in quantum state preparation, a critical step for quantum algorithms.
It introduces ADAPT-GQE, a generative AI framework designed to efficiently synthesize molecular ground states.
This advancement aims to overcome the limitations of iterative algorithms (like ADAPT-VQE) when applied to large molecules in chemistry and materials science.

stories.title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI
stories.author: Tushar Krishna
bullet_points: Introduces TRACE-ROUTER, a new routing mechanism for Agentic AI workflows.
Addresses the limitation of existing routers that make independent, per-call decisions, which fails in long-horizon tasks.
Aims to enable task-consistent and adaptive routing by correctly attributing delayed, task-level feedback to individual LLM routing choices.

stories.title: PinEqualizer: Full Funnel Content Exploration and Debiasing System at Pinterest
stories.author: Zhihua Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces PinEqualizer, a system designed to solve the content cold-start problem in large-scale search and recommender systems.
The solution operates across the entire multi-stage content funnel, applicable to both search and recommendation surfaces.
It effectively reduces inherent bias that favors existing popular content, leading to more accurate predictions across diverse content types.

stories.title: Interpretable EEG biomarkers with bag-of-waves: Spatial and temporal waveform dictionaries for low-data regimes
stories.author: Zhandong Liu
bullet_points: Introduces 'bag-of-waves,' an interpretable framework for analyzing Electroencephalography (EEG) data.
Addresses limitations of traditional EEG analysis (predefined features) and deep learning (lack of interpretability and data hunger).
Aims to provide meaningful, localized waveform dictionaries for neurological diagnosis, especially in low-data scenarios.

stories.title: grapheme-kit: Grapheme-Level Metrics and Text Processing for Multilingual NLP
stories.author: Menan Velayuthan
bullet_points: Introduces 'grapheme-kit,' an open-source Python library to improve text processing in NLP.
Addresses a limitation in existing metrics that rely on Unicode code points, which fail for complex writing systems.
Provides enhanced grapheme cluster processing, specifically for Tamil and Sinhala.

stories.title: A Factorial Study of Synthetic Data Generation for Low-Resource Machine Translation using Grammar Books
stories.author: Rico Sennrich
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of low-resource machine translation for endangered languages lacking parallel data.
Proposes a novel pipeline using LLMs to extract linguistic knowledge (rules, examples, lexicons) from existing grammar books.
Generates synthetic parallel corpora for model fine-tuning, contrasting with prior methods that used grammar content during inference.

stories.title: Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation via Byte-Prefix Marginalization
stories.author: Honggang Qi
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of consolidating open-weight language models from different families into a compact student model.
It introduces Byte-Prefix Marginalization (BPM) to enable cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation (OPD).
BPM solves issues in existing cross-tokenizer methods by preventing the loss or misassignment of teacher probability mass.

stories.title: Biomedical Machine Translation for Low-Resource Arabic-Script Languages via Cross-Lingual Transfer and LoRA Adapter Merging
stories.author: Lifeng Han
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of low-resource Natural Machine Translation (NMT) in biomedical domains for Arabic-script languages.
Employs cross-lingual transfer, using higher-resource languages like Arabic and Persian as pivots to aid translation.
Utilizes LoRA adapter merging for efficient fine-tuning across four severely low-resource target languages (Dari, Pashto, Sorani Kurdish, Urdu).

stories.title: Why Large Language Models and Humans Converge and Diverge in Evaluating Creativity
stories.author: Yingyue Luna Luan
bullet_points: The paper investigates the alignment between Large Language Model (LLM) evaluations of creativity and human judgments.
Findings across six LLMs suggest that LLMs often rely on a narrower set of criteria when evaluating creativity compared to humans.
The research addresses the critical question of when and why LLM judgments converge or diverge from human assessments in creative tasks.

stories.title: From Isolated Tasks to Structured Capabilities: A Multilayer Taxonomy for Large Language Models
stories.author: Yanghua Xiao
bullet_points: The paper addresses the fragmentation in LLM evaluation, which currently organizes evidence by isolated tasks rather than underlying capabilities.
It proposes a novel, multi-layer taxonomy comprising 14 capability domains and 91 subskills.
The taxonomy is structured across Primitive, Constructed, and Integrative layers, guided by principles from human cognitive science.

stories.title: Removing React.js from the codebase and adapting Htmx for UI interactivity
stories.author: Ralfp
bullet_points: The article discusses a shift away from React.js in a codebase.
The replacement technology being adopted for UI interactivity is Htmx.
This represents a trend towards simpler, more traditional web development patterns.

stories.title: Human-in-the-Loop Agentic DevOps: Govern AI Automation in GitHub Issues
stories.author: pwd9000
bullet_points: Focuses on 'Human-in-the-Loop' for Agentic DevOps workflows.
Integrates AI agent confidence, rationales, and human approvals directly into GitHub Issues.
Aims to make AI automation in DevOps processes fast, visible, and human-governed.

stories.title: We Tracked 143,424 AI Citations. Nearly Half Point Back to the Vendors Being Recommended
stories.author: henrik_telle
bullet_points: The article details a study tracking 143,424 AI citations across various large language models (LLMs).
A significant finding is that nearly half of the tracked citations pointed back to the vendors themselves being recommended.
The research was conducted by Orbator, involving queries to models like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity.
